So I probably have a dozen questions regarding equipment but I'll try and keep them minimal.

I have a 6ft St. Croix Avid series medium/fast rod. Good for bass?

I have an older medium/moderate rod I want to use for Catfish. Decent pushbutton reel for under $50 or will I need to spend a little more?

I'd like a bluegill/crappie rod and based on my research I'm thinking 6ft light/fast spinning rod and a reel rated for 6 lb line. I'd use 4lb so I figure I'd want something rated for a little more.

I feel like I'm heading in the right direction with my setups. I have a bunch of questions about lures and techniques but I'll save those for a later time.

The St. Croix will be perfect for bass.

The older medium rod will be good for pretty much anything you're likely to catch in freshwater. As for the reel, I'm assuming by push button you mean spincast (if you mean baitcast then ignore the rest of my comments about the reel.) I never had much luck with them, but I haven't used one in a very long time. It's very likely they've improved immensely in that time. However, if the spincast doesn't work out for you I recommend the Shimano Sedona spinning reel. If that's more than you want to pay, just go to a website like basspro.com and look for reels in your price range with good reviews. There's usually reels that stand out as being popular making it easy to pick the right reel.

For your crappy/bluegill rod. An ultralight would be ideal, but a light rod will be better for a larger range of fish. I have an ultralight for trout and I'm always telling myself I really need to get out and buy a light rod. If I had a light rod I really doubt I'd feel that I needed an ultralight rod. Instead of 6ft, go with 7ft. My ultralight is 7ft and it's made a huge difference in my casting. I can cast further and more accurately.

Hope his helps!

Thanks for the response! Yes I meant spincast. I'm not a huge fan but the rod is meant to have a reel on top (idk how else to explain it) so I guess I'd need a spincast. It's going to be a loaner/beater rod since its already old and beat up I just need a reel.

I personally use a medium-light 6'6" rod with 6lb test for everything from perch and trout to largemouth bass except when targeting larger fish like Northern Pike, Walleye, Muskies, or Salmon. When going for those brutes, I switch over to a medium-heavy with 10-15+ lb line with steel leaders, which I think might also be 6'6".
